items.title: UK economy expands 0.7% in third quarter as AI provides 'extra engine of growth'
items.summary: The U.K. economy grew 0.7% in the third quarter of the year, in line with estimates.
items.body: The U.K. economy grew 0.7% in the third quarter, in line with estimates, driven by output in the services sector. Economists polled by Reuters had expected the economy to grow 0.7% from the previous quarter. The figures showed a slight improvement from the previous quarter, when gross domestic product grew by 0.5%. In the first quarter, the economy grew by 0.6%. The services sector expanded by 0.9%, data from the U.K.'s Office for National Statistics (ONS) showed on Thursday morning. It offset 0.1% output growth in the production sector and a 0.7% contraction in construction. Within the services sector, information and communication was a key driver of growth, expanding by 2.1% in the quarter.

items.title: The rise and fall of Jensen Huang - how the tech superstar became mired in scandal
items.summary: Within days, Huang's status as a seemingly untouchable figure leading the global tech race has crumbled.
items.body: BBC's Samira Hussain reports from Wall Street on what the fall of the tech superstar means. Jensen Huang, known for sporting a black leather jacket to shareholder events, appeared to have it all. He was courted by leaders in the US and China alike, worshipped by investors and seen as a loyal family man. But a rockstar approach to his personal life has ultimately led to his resignation. The 63-year-old has been married since 1985, long before the foundation of Nvidia, the company that propelled him to tech stardom. He is known as a workaholic and a demanding manager, with high standards for those who worked for him, which included his own children, promoted within the company. But he has seen his personal reputation go into freefall this week, undone by romantic entanglements that throw doubt on his focus and his judgement.

items.body: The US stock market steadied itself on Thursday after absorbing big swings for Nvidia’s stock and oil prices. The moves suggested Wall Street sees limited fallout for the artificial intelligence industry, which carries immense influence on the market, despite the sudden fall of one of its biggest evangelists, the Associated Press notes. After dropping nearly 1% at the start of trading, the S+P 500 erased all of the loss and then drifted between small gains and losses before dipping 0.3%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was down 88 points, or 0.2%, with an hour remaining in trading, while the Nasdaq composite was down 0.5% after trimming an early drop of 1.6%. At the center of the swings was Nvidia’s stock. It plunged 14% at the start of trading following the resignation of Jensen Huang, its CEO, co-founder and face of the brand.

items.title: Jensen Huang: Spy row, second affair leaves Nvidia without its rockstar CEO
items.summary: Jensen Huang, who built Nvidia into the world’s dominant AI chipmaker, is stepping down as CEO after a second affair came to light. DW examines how losing its figurehead will affect the firm and the US-China AI race.
items.body: Nvidia's board met late Wednesday to decide on CEO Jensen Huang's future after reports emerged of a second extramarital affair — this time with an employee. In a statement issued on Thursday morning, the world's most valuable chip supplier said Huang was resigning as president, CEO and board member, effective immediately. The firm added that current Vice President and Chief Financial Officer (CFO) Colette Kress would become interim CEO. Under Nvidia's bylaws, Huang can be removed "with or without cause" by a majority vote of its 11 directors. The New York Times first reported on the latest scandal, alleging that the 63-year-old Huang had an affair a senior Nvidia executive who reported directly to him. The latest revelation emerged just three days after Huang admitted a relationship with a Chinese woman, whom United States intelligence agencies believe was spying for China .

items.body: Alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang may have simultaneously owned stakes in businesses in China that benefited Nvidia's biggest competitor in China, Huawei, while she was in business with Nvidia and also reportedly having a romantic affair with its ousted CEO Jensen Huang . The connection between Alice Huang and Huawei was first discovered by analysts at private intelligence firm Tesari. The firm exclusively shared its findings with CNBC. Tesari provides intelligence research to private companies and the U.S. government. This previously unreported entanglement was first uncovered by the research firm which uses artificial intelligence to collect evidence and specializes in national security investigations around the world.

items.title: Who is Nvidia's interim CEO Colette Kress - and who could take over permanently?
items.summary: Chief financial officer Colette Kress in in charge of Nvidia for now, but several others are in the frame as potential successors.
items.body: Nvidia is now facing a scenario few would have considered until very recently - a future without Jensen Huang. The influential co-founder of the AI chip-making giant resigned on Thursday over reports of extramarital affairs, one of which was with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. Chief financial officer Colette Kress is in charge, for now, as the tech giant faces one of its biggest challenges - finding the right person to permanently lead the business that Huang helped create more than three decades ago and turned into one of the world's most valuable companies. Colette Kress has been an industry veteran for more than 30 years, having previously held high positions at tech firms like Cisco and Microsoft.

items.title: Faisal Islam: Why the UK economy is surprisingly resilient
items.summary: The UK is seeing impressive growth, but will it last?
items.body: The UK economy grew at its fastest rate for more than two years in the three months to September. "Top gear" and "strikingly strong" were among the descriptions of the 0.7% growth offered by the economists who track every minor murmur of Britain's economy. It is an upgrade on "solid" and "resilient", and in turn a world away from "hardest hit by the Iran War". Against the backdrop of the world's biggest disruption to energy flows, rising market borrowing costs - and the cruel summers since the pandemic - it is impressive growth. The UK's economic growth has averaged less than 0.1% in the four Q3s [ie July to September] since the pandemic. Even the UK's official forecaster the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR) effectively pencilled in 0.3% at the Budget just 3 weeks ago. This figure has not been exceeded outside the pandemic since 2017.

items.title: UK car industry to press EU for two-year delay to Brexit EV tariffs
items.summary: ‘Rules of origin’ on vehicle batteries due to come into force on 1 January if deal on new delay is not reached Business live – latest updates The UK car industry is preparing to push for a two-year delay to Brexit tariffs on electric cars traded with the EU, after an initial…
items.body: The UK car industry is preparing to push for a two-year delay to Brexit tariffs on electric cars traded with the EU, after an initial European proposal suggested a shorter delay. Tariffs are due to kick in on 1 January for the majority of electric cars traded between the EU and UK unless the two sides can come to an agreement to delay for a second time the implementation of “rules of origin” on batteries. The Brexit deal, which was rushed through on Christmas Eve in 2020, included a clause that British and European electric cars would have to use batteries made in either the UK or the EU with local materials, or face 10% tariffs . The rules would not have existed had the UK remained in the EU.

items.title: Here's what Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress and board chair Harvey Jones wrote to Nvidia employees
items.summary: Interim CEO Colette Kress and board chair Harvey Jones emailed Nvidia employees, expressing gratitude for "resilience, professionalism and continued dedication
items.body: On the heels of founder Jensen Huang's resignation as CEO of Nvidia , new interim CEO Colette Kress and board chair Harvey Jones sent emails to employees Thursday expressing gratitude and optimism for the future. CNBC obtained copies of the emails from a source familiar with the matter, who said Jones sent the first email and Kress replied shortly after. "The Board, Estaff and I recognize that this has been an extraordinarily difficult period and I want you to know how grateful we are for your resilience, professionalism and continued dedication," Kress wrote in her email. The term Estaff is commonly used to refer to executive staff, the group of direct reports to C-suite executives at a company. Nvidia will host a company meeting on November 18 at 9am PST, her email said.

items.title: UK economy grows at fastest rate for more than two years
items.summary: ﻿The UK economy grew by 0.7% in the three months to September, according to official figures.
items.body: ﻿The UK economy grew at its fastest rate for more than two years in the three months to September. Between July and September, the economy expanded by 0.7%, accelerating from the previous three months, official figures , external show. The robust growth suggests a far more resilient economy than expected over the summer, despite the impact of higher energy prices from the Iran war. Strong growth in the services sector - the largest part of the economy, which includes non-physical goods such as consultancy services and computer programming as well as hotels and restaurants - helped boost the numbers. Within services, computer programming registered its fastest growth for the past three years, helped by cloud computing and AI-linked spending. The boost from computer programming and consultancy services has been the biggest driver of growth so far this year.

items.title: From washing dishes at Denny’s to rockstar of AI: the rise and fall of Nvidia’s Jensen Huang
items.summary: Technical expertise and an ability to engage gave the chipmaker’s co-founder, who has now resigned, the edge with customers and investors Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO after alleged affairs Jensen Huang wasn’t always in his trademark leather jacket. When the…
items.body: Jensen Huang wasn’t always in his trademark leather jacket. When the multibillionaire, now former Nvidia chief executive was a teenager in the US, his first job was waiting tables and washing dishes at a branch of Denny’s. “It teaches you humility, it teaches you hard work, it teaches you hospitality,” he said in 2023 of his time at the diner chain. Decades later, having become one of the richest people on the planet, Huang put on a Denny’s apron in tribute to his former employer at an Nvidia event in 2025. By this point Huang had become a rockstar of the artificial intelligence boom – befitting his signature item of clothing – feted around the world by investors, fellow tech executives and politicians. The company that Huang co-founded makes the computer chips that are integral to the development and operation of AI systems such as ChatGPT.

items.title: Jensen Huang's Nvidia exit casts shadow over Wall Street’s $500 billion AI financing bet
items.summary: Nvidia's leadership crisis threatens to spill over into the AI financing boom.
items.body: Leadership change at Nvidia has the potential to threaten financing of the artificial intelligence boom and test Jensen Huang's $500 billion vision to turn AI chips into tradable debt securities. The Nvidia CEO's resignation was announced Thursday following revelations that he had two extramarital affairs — one with an employee and the other with a woman believed by U.S. intelligence to be a Chinese spy . Shares in the tech giant — which has become central to the AI build-out in recent years — initially plunged more than 13% following Huang's resignation, before paring losses. Nvidia has never identified a successor to Huang, who has led the chipmaker since its founding in 1993. Colette Kress, chief financial officer, has been named interim CEO.

items.title: Home sales hit 16-year low in October amid record-high mortgage rates
items.summary: Sales of built units fell to 3.75m in October, down by 8.8% from last year, with mortgage rates at nearly three-year high US existing home sales hit a 16-year low in October as buyers were driven away by record-high mortgage rates and rising inflation, according to new data…
items.body: US existing home sales hit a 16-year low in October as buyers were driven away by record-high mortgage rates and rising inflation, according to new data released on Wednesday. Sales of already built units dropped to 3.75m in October, down by 8.8% from last year, the National Association of Realtors (NAR) reported. The median existing-home sales price increased slightly to $416,700. Declines in sales were seen in the midwest, south and west, though sales in the north-east held steady. Mortgage rates had been steadily declining in 2024 and 2025, with the 30-year rate falling below 6% for the first time in February 2026. But increasing inflation and higher interest rates amid the Iran war have pushed rates back up to a nearly three-year high. The 30-year mortgage rate, which is the most commonly used rate in home loans, is now hovering at about 7.18%, not far from its 2023 high of 7.79%.

items.title: Jensen Huang's exit from Nvidia raises critical questions about the future of AI
items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has been a singular figure in the development of the AI industry, which suddenly has to survive without him.
items.body: Michael Dell described Jensen Huang as a "visionary of the AI age." Deutsche Telekom CEO Tim Höttges said a photo with the Nvidia CEO produced more media coverage for his company than its iPhone launch. During the keynote of his annual Dreamforce conference, Salesforce's Marc Benioff said, "Jensen, we're all following you, bro," as the two paced through the audience. His fame extended way beyond tech. In May, Huang joined President Donald Trump on Air Force One for a trip to China to meet with President Xi Jinping . Three months later, Huang gathered six of the biggest names at the Nasdaq to announce on CNBC a proposed $500 billion artificial intelligence buildout plan, cementing his central role at the intersection of Wall Street and Silicon Valley.

items.title: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say
items.summary: The proposed radical overhaul of the welfare system would move under-25s off the main sickness benefits.
items.body: Some young people could see reductions to the benefits they are entitled to under a radical overhaul of the welfare system to be recommended by a government-commissioned review. As reported in the Times, , external Alan Milburn's year-long report, to be published on Tuesday, is expected to recommend moving under-25s off the main sickness and disability benefits. Milburn, a former Labour health secretary, has been tasked by the government with helping reduce the one in eight 16 to 24 year-olds in the UK who are not in education, employment or training - otherwise known as "Neet". He said on Wednesday night that his plans would not be "pain-free" and would affect both existing and new claimants.

items.title: Metro Bank up for sale, with billionaire investor in line for £420m windfall
items.summary: Shares up 7% after announcement as Jaime Gilinski Bacal seeks exit three years after helping to rescue bank Metro Bank is putting itself up for sale three years after its near-collapse, in a move that could hand a £420m windfall to its Colombian billionaire investor, Jaime…
items.body: Metro Bank is putting itself up for sale three years after its near-collapse, in a move that could hand a £420m windfall to its Colombian billionaire investor, Jaime Gilinski Bacal. Metro Bank made the rare decision to publicly announce it was open to bids on Thursday, paving the way for a wider pool of suitors. The announcement pushed the share price up by 7% by mid-morning, valuing the bank at about £1.3bn. If successful, the sale would allow Gilinski Bacal a chance to sell out of the bank he helped save from near-failure in late 2023. The 68-year-old banking tycoon, who took a seat on Metro’s board after securing a 53% stake three years ago, has already seen a sixfold increase in the value of his shares, which he bought for just 30p each as part of a wider rescue deal.

items.title: AI helps UK economy grow at fastest pace for more than two years
items.summary: GDP ‘grew robustly’ by 0.7% in third quarter and by 0.2% month on month in September despite high oil prices AI helped the UK defy expectations – but will Britain’s resilience fizzle out? Business live – latest updates The UK economy grew by 0.7% in the third quarter, its…
items.body: The UK economy grew by 0.7% in the third quarter, its fastest expansion in two and a half years, as the rollout of AI services increased activity. The Office for National Statistics reported that the economy “grew robustly” in the July to September quarter, almost entirely due to strong and widespread growth in the services sector, led by the IT sector. The quarterly growth rate matched economists’ expectations, and was the fastest recorded since the first three months of 2024, when GDP also rose by 0.7%. In a boost to the chancellor, John Healey, the ONS also said the economy grew by 0.2% in September, though the ONS revised down the growth rate in August from 0.1% to zero. September’s data beat forecasts of zero growth in the month.

items.title: AI is coming for consulting’s billable hours — and its graduate pipeline
items.summary: AI is changing the consulting industry, forcing firms to rethink billable hours and the traditional graduate career ladder.
items.body: Artificial intelligence is challenging the building blocks of the consulting industry, from the fees firms charge clients to the armies of graduates who have traditionally powered its business model. Svilena Tzekova, KPMG's London-based global head of consulting, agreed that the industry is changing. The intellectual property and knowledge that once formed the basis of consulting work are becoming increasingly accessible, she said, so clients have higher expectations than ever before. "Anyone can go and very quickly get to the level of advice that we used to deliver within whatever days or months at times," Tzekova told CNBC. "We were making quite a lot of money by providing advice. I think that part of our business is literally nonexistent anymore." But the industry has yet to work out exactly how to charge for this new kind of work.

items.title: Gas bills to rise as Middle East turmoil persists
items.summary: Gas bills will increase by about 5% from 1 December, Island Energy announces.
items.body: Gas customers in Jersey will see their bills increase by about 5% from 1 December after Island Energy announced a rise in tariffs for households and businesses. The company said its mains gas, mini bulk tank and cylinder tariffs would increase by 1p per kilowatt hour (kWh) for all domestic and commercial customers from 1 December 2026. It said the increase reflected higher wholesale gas and liquefied petroleum gas costs amid disruption to exports and shipping routes in the Middle East after the conflict with Iran. Chief executive Graeme Millar said: "We recognise that any price increase is unwelcome, particularly during winter." Securing fuel at lower prices in advance had limited the impact of wholesale cost increases on customers, Millar said.

items.title: Burberry returns to profit as sales soar, from £85 socks to £9,000 coats
items.summary: CEO says ‘democratic approach’ has helped brand outperform tough market, with big rises in China and US Burberry has returned to profit as its back-to-basics strategy drove strong sales of the British brand’s coats, jackets and handbags over the summer. Joshua Schulman, the…
items.body: Burberry has returned to profit as its back-to-basics strategy drove strong sales of the British brand’s coats, jackets and handbags over the summer. Joshua Schulman, the chief executive, said the luxury brand had outperformed a “challenging luxury market” to achieve sales growth of 6%, helped by strong online and wholesale sales particularly in China and the US. “Our strategy is working,” he said. Burberry said it made a pre-tax profit of £19m in the six months to 26 September after a loss of £48m a year before, as sales rose to £1.1bn. Sales rose 15% in China and 14% in the Americas but fell 1% in the Europe and Middle East region, partly due to the Iran war.

JPMorgan Asset Management's private wealth alternative assets in Asia-Pacific surged 40% over the past 12 months, according to Dan Watkins, the firm's regional chief executive officer, underscoring the growing appetite among high-net-worth and ultra-high-net-worth clients. "So you really have this huge appetite for alternative exposure happening in that ultra-high-net-worth, high-net-worth category," Watkins said recently at a media summit in Singapore.

items.title: Clashes erupt in Barcelona after thousands join Spain general strike
items.summary: Tens of thousands of people have been taking part in the strike, called by the country's main unions over housing and the high cost of living.
items.body: Clashes have broken out between groups of masked men and police in Barcelona after tens of thousands of people took part in Spain's first general strike for 14 years, called by the country's main unions over housing and the high cost of living. Some 120,000 people joined a demonstration in the capital Madrid and more than 50,000 turned out in Barcelona, where footage showed masked men setting fire to rubbish bins and smashing shop windows as police fired tear gas. The head of the big UGT labour union, Pepe Álvarez, said the strike was a success with "massive" participation, while Unai Sordo of the CC OO union said turnout was "very significant." There was a heavy police presence in the centre of Barcelona on Wednesday evening, with officers wearing helmets and riot shields.

items.title: UK drone maker founded by Ukrainians hits £4.5bn value after raising £500m
items.summary: Britain’s national wealth fund invests £113m in UForce, whose equipment has been used heavily in war with Russia A London-based naval drone maker founded by Ukrainians has reached a £4.5bn valuation after it raised more than £500m from investors including the UK government.…
items.body: A London-based naval drone maker founded by Ukrainians has reached a £4.5bn valuation after it raised more than £500m from investors including the UK government. UForce, which makes military drones for land, air and sea, received £113m from the UK’s national wealth fund. The investment makes UForce one of the UK’s fastest-growing unicorns – or startups with a valuation of more than $1bn. Its drones have been used extensively in the war in Ukraine . The UK defence secretary, Wes Streeting, met the UForce chief executive, Oleg Rogynskyy, on Thursday onboard the British aircraft carrier HMS Prince of Wales during a defence conference in Oslo, Norway. items.body: H alf the tech world made up its mind before the facts could be assessed properly. Jensen Huang was “irreplaceable”, said the chorus at the start of this week. Nvidia would melt without the co-founder’s brilliance, apparently. The chipmaker’s board had to find a way to save its genius for the sake of corporate America and the entire AI universe. items.body: I n the Poundland I visit, a treasure trove of bargains, the staff are dejected. The shelves are emptying because the owners have withheld £50m needed for new stock and paying wages. items.body: Can the AI economy survive without its “central bank”? What does Jensen Huang’s fall mean for the world’s second-most valuable company, and what might a tremor in its fortunes mean for the world? Nvidia’s sky-high valuation is based on the fact that it designs and sells the advanced AI chips, called graphics processing units (GPUs), that underpin the AI economy. Without these, AI models such as ChatGPT and Claude could not be trained and would not run. This has made the chipmaker arguably the most important player in AI and, at times, the most valuable company in the world. Huang’s departure sent shares in Nvidia plunging 13% in early trading. items.title: Thanks to American oligarchy, Jensen Huang’s midlife crisis is a problem for all of us | Moira Donegan
items.summary: At a time when individual men wield massive power, the ramifications of the Nvidia CEO’s affair could be enormous One of the reasons you want to distribute power and responsibility in powerful organizations and high-stakes enterprises is so that the narcissism or myopia of one…
items.body: O ne of the reasons you want to distribute power and responsibility in powerful organizations and high-stakes enterprises is so that the narcissism or myopia of one man do not come to carry outsized consequences. When power is spread out across multiple people, it matters less if one of those people is prone to flattery, or in the midst of a midlife crisis, or perhaps just a bit stupid; the limits on his power become limits on the fallout of his character flaws. A broad distribution of authority also has the virtue of making any one man disposable, replaceable: if he turns out to have poor judgement or counterproductive preoccupations, he can be dispensed with, and his role can be filled anew with someone better suited to its responsibilities. But if one man becomes synonymous with a company – or a country – then untold numbers of other people live and die by that man’s decisions.

items.body: O ne thing we all know about the tech billionaires is they are super-smart. We know this largely because they never stop telling us. The “ cognitive elite ”, to use their favoured phrase, are entitled to shape our future without our say-so. When Elon Musk goes hiring, he wants “super-high-IQ small-government revolutionaries”. Long before they got private jets, what fuelled these boys was faith in their own brainpower. As a teenager, Jensen Huang wooed his future wife, Lori, thus: “If you do homework with me every Sunday, I promise you you’ll get straight As.” Which raises the question: if you’re that clever, why act so dumb? The U.S. and China are locked in a race to achieve global AI supremacy, with Washington spending years restricting China's access to Nvidia's most advanced chips to slow its technological progress. Huang was among the loudest voices opposing U.S. strict export controls on advanced chips to China, which has irked some China hawks. The alleged affair with Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen who is not related to him and was reportedly recruited by Chinese intelligence to gather information, has given lawmakers fresh ammunition to push for the inclusion of a series of chip-control measures in this year's National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA).

items.body: U.S. Treasury yields jumped on Thursday, with the 10-year note yield surging above 5%, alongside a move higher in oil prices and expectations of further Federal Reserve hikes. The yield on the 10-year U.S. Treasury note — the benchmark for mortgages, auto loans and credit card debt — rose more than 13 basis points to 5.125%. The 2-year Treasury note yield, more sensitive to short-term Fed interest rate decisions, jumped more than 15 basis points to 4.879%. The longer-dated 30-year Treasury bond yield rose 10 basis points to 5.449%. One basis point equals 0.01%, or 1/100th of 1%, and yields and prices move inversely to one another.
